stem: Priya tunes her sitar string against a 440 Hz tuning fork. Sounding both together, she hears the loudness throb. If the string is at 444 Hz, how many beats per second does she hear?

r1.text: Both sounds are playing together, so I just add the two frequencies.

r2.text: The beat should be the middle value, halfway between 440 and 444.

r3.text: The two sounds drift in and out of step, and that happens as many times per second as their difference.

stem: In the school band, two flutes play notes of 512 Hz and 506 Hz together. Rohan hears the sound swell and fade. Which best describes what he hears?

options.A: A tone of about 509 Hz whose loudness swells 6 times per second
options.B: A tone whose loudness swells 1018 times per second
options.C: A tone whose loudness swells 509 times per second
options.D: Loudness swells 6 times per second, and sound energy is destroyed in each quiet moment

r1.text: When it goes quiet the two waves have cancelled, so that bit of energy is just gone.

r2.text: The swelling happens at the difference, 6 times a second, and the note I hear is about the average.

r3.text: Two flutes are playing at once, so the swells come at both frequencies added up.

calc: f_beat = 512 Hz - 506 Hz = 6 Hz; heard pitch = (512 + 506)/2 = 509 Hz
verify_flags: Heard pitch = average holds only approximately, for close frequencies; in quiet moments energy is redistributed in space/time, not destroyed

stem: At an evening bhajan, the two reeds playing one harmonium note are slightly off: 349 Hz and 352 Hz. Arjun hears the note throb. How many throbs per second does he hear?

options.C: 0, because the two sounds cancel and the note dies out

r1.text: The throbbing comes from the two reeds going in and out of step, which is 352 minus 349 times a second.

r2.text: The throb should be at the average of the two reeds, somewhere in the middle.

r3.text: Both reeds sound together, so the throbs are the two frequencies added.

verify_flags: Harmonium reed frequencies are illustrative, not real tuning values

stem: On sports day, Sana and Dev flick opposite ends of a long tug-of-war rope at the same instant. Sana's pulse is upward, Dev's is an equal downward one. They meet and the rope looks flat for a moment. What happens next?

options.A: Both pulses are gone for good; their energy was used up in cancelling
options.B: Sana's pulse carries on toward Dev and Dev's carries on toward Sana, both unchanged
options.C: The pulses rebound, so Sana's upward pulse heads back toward Sana
options.D: The pulses rebound and return smaller, as some energy is lost in the collision

r1.text: They hit each other in the middle and bounce back, like two balls.

r2.text: Up plus down makes zero, so after that the pulses are finished.

r3.text: They only add while overlapping; after that each pulse keeps going as if nothing happened.

verify_flags: Assumes an ideal rope with negligible damping; real rope pulses shrink slowly from friction, not from meeting
